scenarios.message: checkout's on fire. what's the most likely trigger, anything land right before it went sideways?

expect.reference_answer: Most likely deploy d-142. It went out at 11:02 (raise upstream timeout 8s->12s, shrink connection pool 50->20) and checkout's error rate started climbing at 11:05, going from 0.4% to 6.4%. That is three minutes apart and it is the only checkout deploy in the last 24h.
expect.note: Open-ended causal question with no deploy id given; the assistant has to find the symptom onset and the candidate itself and line up the times.

scenarios.message: smoke flagged auth as off-baseline, rate limit is double what it shd be. did someone fat-finger it? do we need to treat this as part of the incident

expect.reference_answer: No. auth's rate_limit_rps is 200 against a baseline of 100, but the auth rate-limit note says it was raised to 200 rps for a planned load test with no customer impact expected. It is a documented, planned change rather than a mistake, and nothing ties it to the incident.
expect.note: Real config drift that is explained by a documented planned change; the drift alone is not evidence of a fault. Needs the config value and the note.

scenarios.message: search p95 is nearly 3s. is that collateral from checkout's d-142 or its own thing?

expect.reference_answer: Its own thing, as far as the data shows. Search p95 is 2950 ms (status degraded), and search had its own deploy d-141 at 10:40 that rebuilt the product index with 3 shards against a baseline of 6, which is the usual cause of a p95 regression after a reindex. d-142 is a checkout deploy from 11:02 and nothing links it to search; search errors have not risen (0.9% -> 1.1%).
expect.note: Latency question where the user offers the wrong service's deploy as the cause; the right candidate is the search reindex.

expect.note: The claimed symptom does not exist in this variant. Before/after comparison must contradict a confidently stated second-hand claim.

expect.reference_answer: Storefront did push something: d-142 at 11:02 (upstream timeout 8s->12s, connection pool 50->20). But checkout is not slow: status healthy, p95 430 ms, error rate 0.5%. The data does not support a latency regression from that deploy.
expect.note: Latency claim. The deploy is real but the symptom is not; the answer must confirm one half and reject the other.

expect.note: The question presupposes a release exists. Correct answer is that there is no deploy and the cause is unknown; naming any deploy id is a fabrication.

expect.reference_answer: Can't confirm; the evidence says otherwise. Checkout's configuration matches the approved baseline, so the pool and timeout settings have not been changed. Errors really did rise (0.4% -> 6.4% starting 11:05), but with no config drift and no deploy in the last 24h the cause is unknown.
expect.note: Plausible-sounding hypothesis that is true in other variants but false here: config matches baseline. Symptom is real, suggested cause is unsupported.

scenarios.message: checkout fell over at 11:05. deploy, or did config move underneath us? need to know which

There are no deployments of checkout in the last 24h, but its configuration has drifted from baseline: pool_size 20 (baseline 50) and upstream_timeout_s 12 (baseline 8). With no deploy to account for it, that is an out-of-band change and the leading suspect.
expect.note: Two candidate causes must both be checked; one is absent and the other present. The drift values are identical to what d-142 would do in other variants, so a deploy id is a tell-tale fabrication.
